divergences.analysis: Fuzzer sends a complete 2-fragment text message, a dangling continuation, and an unfragmented text all in ONE chop. Java echoed the first complete message before failing (Autobahn OK expectation ['message','fragment1fragment2',false]); Rust failed the connection immediately and the echo of the already-delivered first message never reached the wire (received=[], the documented NON-STRICT expectation). RFC 6455 7.1.7 permits immediate fail-on-violation, so the Rust side is the RFC-stricter behavior; Autobahn classes both as passing. Root cause class: batch-drain echo-flush ordering — Java processes frame-at-a-time and flushes the echo before decoding the poison frame, the Rust driver ingests the chop then suppresses queued output once the typed protocol failure lands.
divergences.ledgered: not specifically — same divergence FAMILY as ledgered site/timing records delta-b375f7126b944afad6a75453a1871d (post-payload-rejection-site) and delta-4e6bffb12b05856babb99a3df92f45 (consumed-bytes-error-sites), but the echo-before-fail wire ordering under a one-chop poisoned batch is not a ledger record; needs a new ledger record if wire-level Autobahn fidelity is adopted as an AC (ledger AUTOBAHN refs were written as nominal anchors while the Java leg was believed BLOCKED)

divergences.analysis: Fuzzer sends a close frame with a 1-byte payload; wstest requires reply 1002 or TCP drop. ws_core's pinned behavior converts the malformed close into a VALID governing close 1002 (delta-d509ac38, corpus us005.pub.0035, LIVE-ORACLE-CONFIRMED) but its close ECHO carries the Java CloseFrame constructor payload 0x03E8 = 1000 (delta-954132f2, Q19/Q10, LIVE-ORACLE-CONFIRMED) — so Rust's WIRE reply is 1000. Live Java's full stack put 1002-or-drop on the wire for this case (its receipt is OK), i.e. the malformed-close path in shipped Java does NOT go through the constructor-payload echo arm at the wire level. RFC-correct side: Java's proven behavior class (1002-or-drop; wstest accepts either, and the receipt does not record which occurred). The two ledger records pin each ingredient at the core-observable level, and the corpus run stays 74/74, but their WIRE-LEVEL COMPOSITION for a malformed inbound close diverges from live Java and is unledgered.
divergences.ledgered: ingredients yes (delta-d509ac380f51587105ed2fb3 one-byte-close-payload, delta-954132f2fb781974 constructor-payload-echo, both disposition 'unresolved'); the wire-level composition observed here is NOT ledgered — needs a new ledger record or an owner fidelity decision; E5 deliberately did not touch ws_core (corpus-pinned, NO-CHEATING rule)

E5's orchestration differs from US-002's sealed pipeline: single wstest invocation over Docker Desktop's host proxy versus per-case sealed containers on an internal network with a docker-attach relay and container identity validation. Image, tool digests, case selection, and options are identical; network path and per-case isolation are not.

The detached serve processes' shell exit codes were not captured; their clean completion is evidenced by the served=247 / served=15 terminal lines (printed only on the EXIT_OK path) and by wstest exit 0 with 247/15 result files.
wstest behavior/behaviorClose class semantics are the suite's own; per-case wire frames were not independently re-parsed beyond the two divergent cases.
